thread:
alex: quick sync — we had a bad rollout of the new scale-plan yesterday that caused repeated pool churn. want to propose a lightweight versioning + rollback playbook for scale plans so we can safely iterate.

karen: yes please. rough idea?

alex: something like: every scale-plan change gets a `plan_id` and `schema_version`, and the operator supports a cheap dry-run and a canary rollout (e.g. 5% of pools). if the canary fails, we auto-roll back to previous plan_id.

priya: one ask: how do we detect "canary fails" reliably? what metrics/alerts?

alex: good q — proposals: 1) spike in evictions > 0.5% over 5m, 2) sustained increase in avg scheduling latency > 30% over baseline, 3) error-rate on allocation RPCs > 1% for 10m. if any triggers, mark plan as degraded.

dmitri: + add unexpected OOMs / kernel panics from node-exporter logs as immediate hard-fail.

karen: can we store plan history in control-plane DB with timestamps + commit message? makes manual rollback easy.

alex: yes — `scale_plans` table: plan_id, parent_plan_id, created_by, commit_msg, schema_version, serialized_rules, canary_fraction, rollout_state. simple rows, immutable append.

priya: operator behavior: when it sees a new plan_id it should run a preflight simulator against recent traffic traces (shadow mode) and surface estimated delta on evictions/latency. if the simulator predicts regression > threshold, mark plan as blocked from rollout.

karen: how heavy is the simulator? we need it cheap.

alex: initial version: sample 5% of requests for 10 minutes, replay scheduling decisions locally, compute delta. it's async and nonblocking. worst-case we skip simulation and require manual approval.

priya: sounds reasonable. for canary rollout, operator picks pools with diverse sizes/tenants. heuristics: small, medium, big and multi-tenant pools.

alex: yes. and rollout steps: `PENDING -> SIMULATED -> CANARY -> GRADUAL -> GLOBAL`. each step has time windows and health checks.

dmitri: we should version operator APIs so old controllers can still read older plan schema. back-compat matters during cluster upgrades.

karen: add a `force_rollforward` flag for SRE to override after manual sign-off (with an audit note).

priya: for rollback playbook: automated rollback if canary fails. manual rollback steps in runbook: 1) identify plan_id, 2) `set_active_plan(previous_plan_id)`, 3) monitor pools for 15m, 4) if stable, tag bad plan as `rejected`. include sample `kubectl` commands in runbook.

alex: include a safety window: when switching plans, operator performs a graceful drain-suppression (delay aggressive preemptions for X sec) to avoid thrash.

dmitri: what about in-flight lease accounting? switching plans might change admission rules and invalidate outstanding intents. operator must fence new admissions until state reconcile completes. add `reconcile_epoch` in plan metadata.

karen: good call. add a `plan_epoch` that increments. operator refuses to accept new tenant tokens from older epoch.

deploy-bot: deployment started for `operator:v2.18` — canary fraction default=0.05 — trace=scaleplan-v2.

alex: note for rollouts: keep a shadow copy of previous active plan and keep it immediately reapplicable (no migrations) so rollback is constant time.

priya: monitoring panels to add: per-pool churn rate, avg scheduling latency, allocation RPC error %; a plan-compare dashboard that shows delta vs baseline.

karen: and an alerting playbook: P0 if eviction spike + allocation errors, P1 for latency regressions. include `@oncall` escalation path.

dmitri: infra ops should add RBAC binding so only `infra:scale-admins` can `force_rollforward`/`reject_plan`.

alex: final implementation notes: 1) minimal schema v1, 2) operator implements simulator toggle, 3) add DB table and admin UI to list plan history, 4) runbook doc + alerting.

priya: i'll draft the RFC follow-up with mockups for plan-history UI and the sample rollbacks commands.

karen: i'll own the runbook and the alert rules. dmitri, can you add the plan_epoch fwd/back compat checks to operator?

dmitri: yep, will add a small state-machine test and e2e that flips plans and asserts no thrash.

alex: awesome — thanks all. can we sync tomorrow 09:30 for 20m?

karen: works for me.

priya: added to calendar.

deploy-bot: deployment `operator:v2.18` finished (canary pools: 12).
